Q: Omit headers in requests POST request A:

You can create a PreparedRequest and then edit its headers before sending it. This is unlikely to help—but it may be worth doing just to convince yourself, so…

Instead of this:

r = requests.post(url, headers = {"Content-Type" : "text/zinc; charset=utf-8"}, \
                  cookies = {"cookie":cookie}, \
                  data = data)

Do this:

sess = requests.Session()
req = requests.Request('GET', url, 
                       headers={"Content-Type": "text/zinc; charset=utf-8"},
                       cookies={"cookie": cookie},
                       data=data)
preq = req.prepare()
preq.headers = {key: value for key, value in preq.headers.items()
                if key in {'Content-Type', 'Cookie'}}
r = sess.send(preq)

It's in prepare that all the changes get done. You obviously want to keep the cookies being turned into a Cookie header, but you don't want to keep any of the other changes, so I just removed any header besides the one you explicitly passed and Cookie.

Q: Python requests remove the Content-Length header from POST A:

You'll have to prepare the request manually, then remove the generated content-length header:

from requests import Request, Session

s = Session()
req = Request('POST', url, data=data)
prepped = req.prepare()
del prepped.headers['content-length']
response = s.send(prepped)

Do note that most compliant HTTP servers may then ignore your post body!

If you meant to use chunked transfer encoding (where you don't have to send a content length), then use a iterator for the data parameter. See Chunked-Encoded Requests in the documentation. No Content-Length header will be set in that case.

Q: Mysql query to show records with 3 date criterias A:

So I need to display records only where

  • The match_date is either today or in the future
match_date   >= CURRENT_DATE()
  • The release_date has been triggered IE the date is today or in the future
release_date >= CURRENT_DATE()
  • The remove_date has not been reached.
CURRENT_DATE() < remove_date

The query should be,

SELECT * 
FROM competition_matches  
WHERE match_date   >= CURRENT_DATE() 
AND release_date >= CURRENT_DATE()  
AND CURRENT_DATE() < remove_date   
AND gender='Male'
ORDER by match_date ASC LIMIT 3;

but in the data example there should be none in the result because release_date are all '2026-01-22'
